what_this_is: A DECLARATION PER NAME, clustered. Every entry is a published name of
tests/fixtures/public_api_snapshot.json that does not resolve in the live tree, with
the kind of non-resolution and the reason. tests/test_public_api_accountability.py is
red on a recorded name that neither resolves nor appears here.
MEMBERSHIP IS FROZEN AND IS NOT A RULE EVALUATED AT GATE TIME. Each cluster carries
the rule it was assigned by so the judgement is auditable, but the gate reads only the
name lists. A name that stops resolving tomorrow is therefore RED even where a rule
here would have had an opinion about it -- which is the whole obligation: a removal is
loud. A cluster that assigned membership live would silence the next one automatically.
AND THE SNAPSHOT IS NOT AN INPUT TO THE ALIAS LAYER (owner, 2026-11-19). It says WHICH
names existed, not what they should alias TO. Nothing here emits a binding; a cluster
whose kind is RENAMED-NOT-YET-BOUND records an open hole and does not close it.
ADDING A ROW IS A JUDGEMENT, NOT A CHORE. scripts/public_api_accountability.py
--propose gathers the evidence and suggests a cluster; a name you cannot place stays
RED. A declaration written to silence a name nobody understood reads as a decision
later, which is worse than the gap -- CLAUDE.md's opening rule is this hazard from the

the_tree_the_snapshot_recorded.why_it_matters: The snapshot is a recording of datamodel-code-generator's tree taken the day before that tree was deliberately removed, so 639134c75^ holds the actual class statement for every recorded name. Rules below that cite a 'recorded definition' read it there rather than inferring from the spelling.

kinds.NAMESPACE-RETIRED: the recording namespace is gone from the live tree
kinds.SAME-WORD-NEW-PATH: the word and the object are unchanged; the import path moved, and the declaration names where to
kinds.POSITIONAL-INDEX-NOT-A-NAME: the word's distinguishing content was a generator traversal index; rebuild-plan.md SS4's own words
kinds.DOCUMENT-NO-WORD-NO-IDENTITY: the document states the node; no word of ours identifies it, because it is not a subject and gets no class
kinds.NO-DOCUMENT-NO-SUBJECT: no document of the pinned bundle is behind the word at all
kinds.RETIRED-DOCUMENT: the document the class compiled from is gone from the pinned bundle
kinds.RENAMED: the subject is in the tree under a different word, and no alias is owed for this one
kinds.RENAMED-NOT-YET-BOUND: the subject is in the tree under a different word, nothing binds the published one, and THAT IS AN OPEN HOLE -- an adopter's import fails today

clusters.rule: the word carries a terminal numeric suffix and its document is still emitted
clusters.reason: AuthorizedAgents20, AcceptProposalResponse4, Action11: the digit is datamodel-code-generator's traversal order, not a fact about the node. CLAUDE.md states the hazard -- 'Codegen variant numbering is unstable ... adding or reordering even one sibling schema shifts the entire numbering window' -- and rebuild-plan.md SS4 states the rule our compiler follows instead: 'A POSITIONAL INDEX IS A DECLARED PLACEHOLDER, NOT A NAME', gated by tests_emit/test_no_positional_name_is_public.py over the whole symbol. A word whose only content is a position is therefore not owed; the stable spelling is, and that is what aliases.py serves. Every name here had its document checked: all are still in schemas/cache/3.2 and still emitted.
clusters.stated_in: CLAUDE.md -> Codegen variant numbering is unstable; docs/plan/rebuild-plan.md SS4

clusters.rule: the class definition at 639134c75^ subclassed StrEnum/Enum/ScalarStr/ScalarInt/ScalarFloat/RootModel, and no class in the live tree carries the word
clusters.reason: Read off the recorded tree, not inferred: ME, GBEnum and CAEnum were class X(StrEnum) for the per-country items enums of core/postal-area-support.json, and Criterion and TmpxMacro were class X(ScalarStr). Our compiler lowers both -- an anonymous enum to Literal[...] on the field it is stated at, a constrained scalar to a named constraint annotation (rebuild-plan.md SS2 'Constraints bind to the type, not the field'). The node is still compiled and its acceptance still graded; there is no class, so there is no object an alias could name. WHAT THIS DOES NOT CLAIM: that the name was worthless to an adopter. 30 of these were published at adcp.types and an adopter who annotated with one breaks, and no alias can fix it -- that set is listed on adcp-client-python-5wr6 for the owner.

clusters.rule: the word (or, for an alias entry, its recorded target) is pascal_case of a property, definitions, $defs or required key stated by the recorded document or a document it $refs, and no class in the live tree carries the word
clusters.reason: Align, Button, Card, AllowedInterval, AuthorizedAgents1: the old generator minted a class per anonymous inner NODE and named it from the property key. rebuild-plan.md SS4's decision is 'One class per SUBJECT, not per position', and an anonymous object or enum under a property is not a subject -- so the compiler lowers it into the parent's annotation or emits it in its own document's module under a path-qualified name. The $ref closure is transitive BECAUSE THE OLD MODULE WAS: datamodel-code-generator inlined every $ref target into the entry document's module, which is how Art9Basis and Onboarder came to be recorded under signals/get-signals-response while core/signal-definition.json is what states them. WHAT THIS DOES NOT ESTABLISH, and the limit is deliberate: for the 53 whose recorded base was AdCPBaseModel the node may well be emitted under a path-qualified name that this rule does not identify. It says the WORD names no subject the tree binds, not that the node vanished -- the node's acceptance is graded by the contract gate either way.
clusters.stated_in: docs/plan/rebuild-plan.md SS4 -> What becomes what, and -> Names
